candidates: When migrating a calculator from `FileIOCalculator` to `GenericFileIOCalculator`, include explicit backward-compatibility hooks: (1) accept the old `command` keyword and immediately raise a `RuntimeError` (or `FutureWarning`) that includes precise migration instructions (e.g. 'use `CalcProfile(command=...)` and pass it as `profile=`'), and (2) detect any legacy `ASE_<CALC>_COMMAND` environment variable that is set and emit a `FutureWarning` directing users to the new `profile=` API. Use the `Espresso` calculator as the canonical reference implementation of this pattern.

When porting a widely-used calculator (e.g. Siesta, GPAW) from `FileIOCalculator` to `GenericFileIOCalculator`, prefer a conservative migration strategy—introduce the new implementation under a new class name or in a separate module—rather than replacing the existing class in-place, to avoid breaking a large user base. In-place replacement (as done for lower-traffic calculators like ELK) is acceptable only when the user base is known to be small.
